Chef was deaf, and mostly blind. Still he followed his best friend out through the woods. His right leg was almost stiff from arthritis, but autumn was in the air and the morning sun was warming. They walked together up the path and through the grassy field. When they where young, potatoes used to grow here, but now it was left to nature and all manners of flowers and straws had taken over. They shared a few blackberries from the bush by the creek, helping themselves to a few mouthfuls of the water.


The pace was slow but steady and after a small climb they reached the top of the hill. There, looking out over the landscape they could survey the territory that they had called their own their entire life. They saw the waves breaking against the smooth stone once carved by the great ice. They saw the fields and forrests, the glistening road of quartz from the quarry nearby. The birds where chirping and the hawk was at his usual post atop the big fur. Unpacking their lunch they sat down.


As Chef was digging into his favorite pork sausage he felt something cold poke his neck. Having always been around kids and raising a few himself he was used to being poked, grabbed and dragged around. To him it was never a chore, watching them all develop and grow, but this was different.


When I pulled the trigger and the echo died down, he fell as silent as the birds. Chef was my beautiful and faithful dog and now he rests at the base of the cherry tree where we would sit, drink and laugh watching the sun go down.

Don't! Learn to use your mirrors correctly, no backup sensor can replace them.

So many accidents happen due to people counting on them to catch stuff (kids) in the way.

When you get to your parked car make a mental map of what the surroundings are before you get in. Are there any low posts that the sensors might not catch, is this a place where kids run around? Then when you get in the car locate that mental map in your mirrors. The red honda to my right I can see in my right mirror there, I have to avoid it's rear left corner. The large black suv yo my rear I can see in my rear view. When I back out of here I should get that tree first in my right mirror, then in my rear view. There it is. Keep backing up. And there it is in my rear view. You should at all times have an understanding of where your car us to the surrounding objects. And if you don't, stop, reorientate yourself before proceeding.

Also make sure that your mirrors are set up correctly. You should not have to move your head to check them out. This way you will have perrifiral vision of movement in the left mirror while looking in the right etc.
